steps.title: Build one row per customer ID that placed an order
steps.change: These are the candidate counts before the cutoff. The learner's COALESCE also supplies the fallback when a matched customer's name has a NULL part.
steps.added_sql:
WITH customer_counts AS (
    SELECT
        o.CustomerID,
        COALESCE(c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName, 'Unknown customer') AS customer_name,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS orders_placed
    FROM Orders AS o
    LEFT JOIN Customers AS c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
    GROUP BY o.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
)
SELECT * FROM customer_counts
ORDER BY orders_placed DESC, CustomerID ASC;

steps.title: Find the fifth row's count
steps.added_sql:
SELECT COALESCE((SELECT orders_placed FROM customer_counts
                 ORDER BY orders_placed DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4), 0) AS cutoff;

steps.title: Keep everyone who meets the cutoff and sort
steps.change: The >= comparison includes everyone tied at the cutoff. CustomerID controls the display order of ties.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT CustomerID, customer_name, orders_placed
FROM customer_counts
WHERE orders_placed >= COALESCE(
    (
        SELECT orders_placed
        FROM customer_counts
        ORDER BY orders_placed DESC
        LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4
    ),
    0
)
ORDER BY orders_placed DESC, CustomerID ASC;
